The majority voted against an [amendment](http://www.openaustralia.org/debates/?id=2006-02-16.18.2) introduced by Liberal MP [Jackie Kelly](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/mp.php?mpn=Jackie_Kelly&mpc=Lindsay&house=representatives), which means that it was rejected. The amendment would have amended the original motion "That this bill be now read a second time" with the following: _That all words after “That” be omitted with a view to substituting the following words: “the House is of the opinion that the bill is unacceptable in its current form and the preferred policy approach should be:_ _(1) the Minister for Health and Ageing continuing to have the decision making role in relation to the approval of _restricted goods_ as defined in the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989;_ _(2) the Minister being required to obtain written advice from the Therapeutic Goods Administration prior to giving written approval or refusal to approve; and_ _(3) the Minister’s decision being subject to disallowance by each House of Parliament”._ This division was a [conscience vote](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/faq.php#rebelandfree), meaning that members were not required to vote along party lines. _Background to the bill_ The bill was introduced to amend the [Therapeutic Goods Act 1989](http://www.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/tga1989191/) in order to transfer the responsibility for regulatory approval of [RU486](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RU486) from the Minister for Health and Ageing to the [Therapeutic Goods Administration](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Therapeutic_Goods_Administration). The majority voted against [amendments](http://www.openaustralia.org/debates/?id=2006-02-16.40.1) introduced by Liberal MP [Andrew Laming](http://publicwhip-rails.openaustraliafoundation.org.au/mp.php?mpn=Andrew_Laming&mpc=Bowman&house=representatives). These amendments opposed the main purpose of this bill, which is to remove ministerial responsibility for approval of RU486 and related medicines. Instead, the amendments would have made some changes to the current process but fundamentally kept it in place. In other words, ultimate responsibility for approving RU486 would remain with the Minister. speeches.speaker: Gary Humphries
speeches.brief: The committee report on the Therapeutic Goods Amendment (Repeal of Ministerial responsibility for approval of RU486) Bill 2005 was presented and ordered to be printed.

speeches.speaker: Fiona Nash
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the bill to remove ministerial responsibility for approving RU486 and return it to the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) is about proper assessment of the drug's safety, not about abortion, and noted that RU486 is approved in 35 countries including the US, UK, and New Zealand, and that the bill is co-sponsored by senators from four parties.

speeches.speaker: Sandy Macdonald
speeches.brief: The Senate passed the second reading of the Therapeutic Goods Amendment (Repeal of Ministerial responsibility for approval of RU486) Bill 2005, which would transfer approval of the abortifacient drug RU486 from the health minister to the Therapeutic Goods Administration. speeches.speaker: Guy Barnett
speeches.brief: Amendments were foreshadowed to replace the repeal of ministerial responsibility for approving RU486 with conditions requiring the Minister to seek advice from the Australian Health Ethics Committee, provide written reasons, and make approvals or refusals disallowable legislative instruments. The speaker also proposed a procedure for dealing with two sets of amendments in committee.

speeches.speaker: John Hogg
speeches.brief: Senator Barnett moved amendments requiring the Minister for Health to seek written advice from the Australian Health Ethics Committee, prepare a statement of reasons, and make any approval or refusal a disallowable legislative instrument for parliamentary oversight. He argued the decision on RU486 should ultimately rest with elected representatives rather than a single minister.

speeches.speaker: Fiona Nash
speeches.brief: The Senate passed the bill removing ministerial responsibility for approval of RU486 and transferring that authority to the Therapeutic Goods Administration. Opponents argued the drug is a “killer drug” that terminates pregnancy and that the TGA cannot consider social or ethical consequences, while supporters said medical experts should make the decision rather than politicians.
